correctness.rationale: For \(n=2^ap^b\), powerfulness and non-perfect-power reduce to \(a,b\ge2\) and \(\gcd(a,b)=1\). The totient has exponent vector \((a+t-1,b-1,c_1,\ldots,c_r)\), so its Achilles condition gives exactly \(b\ge3\), all \(c_j\ge2\), and the second gcd condition. For fixed \(p\), exponent pairs lie in a logarithmic triangle. At a prime \(\ell\nmid g\), only the residue pair \((0,0)\) is excluded; at \(\ell\mid g\), the distinct pair \((1-t,1)\) is additionally excluded, producing the stated Euler product. When the odd part is absent, both exclusions occur at every prime. A fresh computation of the universal product through primes below \(100000\) gave \(0.322634616605\), consistent with the submitted constant.
